Preface

In contemporary enterprise and organizational environments, efficient information technology administration forms the backbone of operational productivity. However, small-to-medium enterprises and institutions frequently rely on disconnected spreadsheets, manual paper logbooks, and informal communication channels to track physical computers, monitor software license expirations, and address employee technical faults. This disjointed approach inevitably produces unrecovered hardware assets, non-compliance penalties from unmonitored license quotas, and unfulfilled support service level agreements (SLAs).

The “IT Asset & Support Desk Management System” (code name: AssetDesk) was developed as an end-to-end, full-stack web engineering project to solve these operational pain points through a centralized, role-based platform. This report documents the complete systems development lifecycle (SDLC) of the application, structured systematically into the following chapters:

  • Chapter 1 (Introduction): Presents the institutional profile of VICAIT, the host industry environment, and core project specifications.
  • Chapter 2 (Proposed System): Outlines system scope, operational benefits, and technical, economic, and operational feasibility assessments.
  • Chapter 3 (System Analysis): Documents existing system deficiencies, IEEE-830 functional requirements (FR-01..FR-20), non-functional constraints, and structured DFD flow models.
  • Chapter 4 (System Planning): Details the 15-week milestone roadmap and Gantt scheduling.
  • Chapter 5 (Tools & Environment): Outlines the verified hardware specifications, runtime versions, and software dependencies.
  • Chapter 6 (Design & Implementation): Explains the 3-tier architecture, ER/Class models, database collections, and core source code logic.
  • Chapter 7 (System Testing): Reports real test execution results across 272 automated test cases, code coverage metrics, and API latency benchmarks.
  • Chapters 8 & 9 (Limitations & Future Scope): Discusses technical boundary conditions and roadmap enhancements.
  • Chapter 10 (References): Lists authoritative academic, technical, and web standard citations.

The reader will find a transparent, fully reproducible engineering documentation set that bridges academic software engineering principles with real-world enterprise requirements.
